scope: Native ARM64 ZealC compiler, locked pointer updates; UTM-bundled QEMU with HVF, one virtual CPU
failure: The unmodified installed candidate returned 1 when a locked U32 pointer increment should have carried 0x0000ffff to 0x00010000. A separate check returned 1 for unsigned U16 arithmetic above its sign bit.
change: Use a 32-bit store-exclusive for 32-bit locked updates and select unsigned zero-extension by U16/U32 type in both supported indirect-address modes.
result: On a disposable copy of the candidate disk with the rebuilt kernel, the carry/adjacent-word check and a combined unsigned U16/U32 and existing I64 lock check each returned 42. The copied kernel was read back with an identical SHA-256.
test: tests/compat/LockWidthRuntime.ZC; make check-lock-width reproduces the combined test against a built image.
limitations: Single-vCPU execution does not prove atomicity under contention or SMP support.
The test exercises pointer updates and does not exhaust all locked operators or addressing modes.
No live UTM window or physical Pi verification; the Pi card and installed candidate disk were not modified.
This does not implement the pinned scheduler or address MessageScan behavior.

increment_decrement_followup.before: The width-fixed kernel returned 1: a locked postfix increment through an I64 pointer did not update the target.
increment_decrement_followup.change: Use the loaded value instead of the address in the exclusive increment/decrement loop. Preserve the loaded value as the postfix expression result and the computed value as the prefix result.
increment_decrement_followup.after: The initial I64 increment/decrement and return-value probe returned 42. A separate combined run of U16, U32, and I64 increment cases, the width/carry checks, and the existing I64 lock check returned 42 and reset the compiler.
increment_decrement_followup.limits: One virtual CPU and pointer-address cases only; no proof of exclusive retry under contention, SMP, all operand widths/operators, live UTM, or Pi hardware.

instruction_encoding_followup.baseline: Instruction inspection returned 1 on the prior candidate because store-exclusive status overlapped data; functional QEMU results alone did not reveal the architecturally constrained encoding.
instruction_encoding_followup.first_change: Resolve the target address before the retry loop and use marked-clobbered x16 as a distinct store-exclusive status register; branch on x16 back to the exclusive load.
instruction_encoding_followup.acquire_negative_control: After that change, instruction inspection returned 5 because the helper named LDAXR emitted the non-acquire LDXR encoding. LLVM llvm-mc independently gave ldaxr x0,[x1] as c85ffc20 and ldxr x0,[x1] as c85f7c20.
instruction_encoding_followup.final_change: Encode the load-acquire bit in the exclusive-load helper.
instruction_encoding_followup.final_result: Combined functional regression and generated-instruction inspection returned 42. The check verifies distinct status/data/base registers, a backward retry to a same-width acquire exclusive load and the same base register for the selected generated function.
instruction_encoding_followup.limits: One virtual CPU: encoding inspection and functional execution do not prove real SMP contention, all code-generation cases, or live UTM/Pi behavior. The Pi card and original candidate disk were not modified.

parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.initial_observation: A simple instruction inspection found no ordinary memory accesses inside its exclusive window; it did not reproduce the potential spill problem.
parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.negative_control: A function-call argument containing a locked postfix update produced no store-exclusive instruction on the previous kernel; the instruction check returned 102 (100 + missing instruction).
parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.parser_change: Mark the newly inserted instruction-list nodes for each lock statement instead of marking pre-existing nodes. The list inserts new nodes immediately after the head.
parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.backend_change: Move publication of prefix, postfix, and compound-update expression results after the successful store-exclusive; preserve the postfix old value in a register on each retry.
parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.result: On the rebuilt one-vCPU UTM QEMU framework candidate, the combined regression returned 42. It checks nested postfix in a function call, prefix/postfix values, unsigned widths, acquire/release encodings, retry target, and no ordinary memory operations between the tested exclusive pair. A separate boundary case verifies exactly two exclusive stores for adjacent braced and unbraced lock statements, with ordinary increments surrounding them.
parser_and_exclusive_window_followup.limits: Instruction inspection covers the tested generated functions, not every expression or operator. No forced exclusive-store failure, multicore contention, live UTM window, or physical Pi test. Source and installed candidate disk remained unchanged on hardware.

global_local_address_followup.before: The preceding kernel returned 3302: functional global updates ran but the instruction check did not find the two required store-exclusive operations.
global_local_address_followup.change: Reuse address normalization for static, frame, and absolute-pointer lvalues in prefix, postfix, constant compound, and nonconstant compound locked paths.
global_local_address_followup.after: UTM-framework QEMU returned 42 for global and address-exposed stack-local compound increment and postfix increment, including instruction inspection; prior pointer, signedness, width, and parser-boundary checks also passed. A separate TaskMessageSchedulingChecks returned 42.
global_local_address_followup.limits: Single-vCPU tests with selected integer operators; do not establish forced exclusive failure, multicore contention, all address modes, actual live UTM or physical Pi behavior. MessageScan and scheduler implementation were not modified.
